BaselineTestingRules.Mission: Language- and framework-neutral testing baseline selected by actual test-role facts, including explicit project languages. Runner-specific instructions are separate layers; this baseline does not depend on the TypeScript-specific testing-common layer or choose a runner. Rules are agent instructions, not a second command pipeline. Only the configured selector/DAG determines authority gates; examples below are not defaults and must not be run as extra gates.

BeliefState.Axiom: One test checks one behavior, named after that behavior — not after the function. A test named `retries_until_success_then_stops` documents intent; `test_retry_2` documents nothing. The name is the specification a reader trusts without opening the body.

A test gives the same verdict on every run. No dependence on wall-clock time, random seeds, ordering between tests, or ambient environment. Inject the clock, fix the seed, control the input. A flaky test is a failing test.

A unit test touches no network, no real filesystem outside a temp dir, no shared mutable global, and no other test's state. External collaborators are faked at the boundary. What needs the real world is an integration test, named and gated as one.

A test reads as arrange → act → assert, with the assertion on the behavior's observable outcome, not on internal calls. Assert the returned value / raised error / recorded effect — not "method X was invoked", unless the interaction itself is the contract.

The failure paths are tested, not only the happy path. For each documented error mode there is a test that provokes it and asserts the specific error. Untested error handling is unverified error handling.

AntiPattern.Bad: `test_parse`, `test_parse_2`, `test_parse_edge` — names that index the function, not the behavior under test.
Asserting on `now()`, real `sleep`, unseeded randomness, or the order tests happen to run in.
AntiPattern.Instead: Inject the clock/seed; assert bounds or exact controlled values.

AntiPattern.Bad: A unit test that opens a socket, calls a live API, or writes outside a temp directory.
AntiPattern.Instead: Fake the boundary; move a genuine end-to-end check into a separate, gated integration test.

AntiPattern.Bad: Asserting a private helper was called, or snapshotting an internal structure, so a valid refactor breaks the test.
AntiPattern.Instead: Assert the observable outcome the caller depends on.

Hook.Purpose: The behavior's tests pass via the project's declared runner and configured selector/DAG.
Hook.Expected: Actual required-step success with changed behavior tests present; use the workflow owner's reviewed invocation.

Hook.Purpose: No silently disabled tests are shipped as coverage.
Hook.Example: Review changed tests for skip, xfail, t.Skip, it.only, fdescribe and .only(.
Hook.Expected: No focus-only tests; each real deferred skip has a ticket reference. This example creates no command gate.

BaselineTestingRules.RewardCriteria: ✅ Each test checks one behavior and is named after that behavior. ✅ Deterministic: clock/seed injected, no cross-test ordering dependence. ✅ Isolated: no network, no real FS outside a temp dir, no shared global; boundaries faked. ✅ Arrange → act → assert; assertion on the observable outcome. ✅ Every documented failure mode has a test that provokes it and asserts the specific error. ❌ Tests named after the function (`test_parse_2`) rather than the behavior. ❌ Dependence on real time, unseeded randomness, or run order. ❌ A unit test that touches the network, live services, or the real filesystem. ❌ Assertions on internal mechanics that a valid refactor would break. ❌ Disabled/skipped tests shipped without a referenced reason.
